_comment: Three rounds of one class, all on ONE file, and the findings name nothing that file's imports export. With a single flagged file there is no shared import to measure, so the seam is whichever import ranks first — a guess. Modelled on a real case where the guess landed on a logging-adjacent module while the invariant lived in another import entirely. It must be reported and not gated: no diff the fix makes would touch the guess.

findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the decision atomic with what is pushed**

The verdict is taken before the lock is held, so a concurrent writer can change what the call sends after it was judged. Nothing revalidates it, so the race stands.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate the ref along with the revision**

The revision is compared but the ref is not, so a concurrent writer pointing another ref at the same revision passes this check unchanged. Nothing revalidates it, so the race stands.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Judge the identity that was captured**

The reads still follow ambient state rather than the identity captured up front, so the verdict can describe something the call will not send. A concurrent writer wins the race unless this is revalidated.
